title: Open the Board from the verified Git trunk

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-430#open-the-board-from-the-verified-git-trunk at e4faafbdbde434438d5c7d0d76f1fe9137dc00c5

Verdict: Caught.

Promise (caller suggestion validated against the seed's Scope paragraph): "An unavailable origin, a missing trunk, an unreadable backlog, or a fetched commit other than the verified one cannot establish a Board, and nothing falls back to GitHub REST membership. With no Board shown, the failure is shown as unavailable."

Fault (the suggested one, applied as written): in dashboard/server/performedRefRead.ts `performVerifiedTrunkRead`, whenever the shared check answered a non-verified trunk (unavailable, rejected, missing-trunk, unreadable-backlog), the read fell back to REST: `resolveRevisionViaGh(source.repository, source.ref, signal)`, then `readRepositoryFileViaGh(source.repository, source.backlogPath, revision, signal)`, recorded that revision as observed and answered backlog, and answered the Board from it. Fixtures and assertions were unchanged. Typecheck (tsc -p dashboard/tsconfig.json) was clean.

Checks examined: e2e/observation/read-failure.spec.ts and e2e/observation/transient-read-exclusions.spec.ts (13 tests), and dashboard/backend-tests/runtime/first-open-waits-for-read.spec.ts (4 tests). Commands were the caller's focused Playwright command and `npm run --silent test:dashboard:backend --` command. Counts come from the proof-record JSON.

Evidence:
- Baseline in an isolated detached scratch worktree at the revision (clean status, npm ci, Node 24.21.0): e2e 13/13 expected; backend 4/4 expected.
- Faulted: e2e 6 failed, 7 passed; backend 1 failed, 3 passed.
- Wrong Board, independently observed: in "read failure and retry publishes the first snapshot … after failed openings" (read-failure.spec.ts:163), Git was disconnected through `origin.disconnectGit()`. The page snapshot at failure (Playwright error-context) shows a status "Published work read at revision d4cec31" and the Board region, so REST established a Board while origin was unreachable. Caught by `expectProblemAndNoSnapshot` (dashboard/test-support/dashboardPage.ts:191, the `problem` alert "Published work could not be read" assertion), called at read-failure.spec.ts:182.
- REST fallback reached, independently observed in the failure copy: the shown problem text came from REST reads, not from the Git check. With unreachable origin or a missing trunk, it read "The published backlog could not be interpreted … found 0 \"## Taken\"": the fake REST backlog content was read and parsed. With an unreadable backlog, it read "GitHub answered HTTP 404 … while reading main": the REST `ref main` was asked. In each case the unavailable copy was replaced. The expected-text assertions in `expectProblemAndNoSnapshot` caught this at read-failure.spec.ts:111 (Git unreachable though REST would answer), read-failure.spec.ts:128 (unreadable backlog), transient-read-exclusions.spec.ts:65 (missing trunk), transient-read-exclusions.spec.ts:81 (unreadable backlog) and transient-read-exclusions.spec.ts:136 (switching project during an unreachable-origin wait). The backend check failed the same way at first-open-waits-for-read.spec.ts:87 (missing trunk copy replaced by REST-read interpretation copy).
- Each of these tests also ends with `expect(restMembershipAsked(...)).toEqual([])`. In every faulted case, an earlier copy or no-snapshot assertion failed first, so that final REST-membership assertion was not the one observed catching.
- Claim limit: the observed paths are unreachable origin, missing trunk and unreadable backlog on the cold open. The "fetched commit other than the verified one" (rejected) branch was faulted by the same edit, but no examined test was confirmed to exercise it.

Restoration: `git checkout -- dashboard/server/performedRefRead.ts`. After that, `git diff --quiet HEAD` was clean and `git status --porcelain` was empty, matching the pre-probe state. The same commands passed after restoration: e2e 13/13 expected, backend 4/4 expected. The scratch worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force`; no ic-scratch entry remains in the worktree list. The execution checkout and the git stash were not touched.

Next proof action: none needed for the observed paths. Optionally, confirm a maintained check that reaches the "fetched commit other than the verified one" outcome on the Board's cold open, if the caller wants that branch covered by name. This probe made no new repair decision, and this evidence matches no already-planned repair.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, wall-clock seconds of the focused commands under load average ~15): baseline e2e 83 s + backend 40 s; faulted e2e 85 s + backend 23 s; restored e2e 27 s + backend 17 s; total about 275 s.
- Human effort: unavailable; no human time was spent or measured in this invocation.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a separately supported measure; about 20 tool calls (count, estimated from this session).

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 391570 ms (measured), from 1795765405000 to 1795765796570 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Invocation start: 2026-11-27T07:43:25Z. Invocation end: 2026-11-27T07:49:56.570Z (the report finisher's sample).

Wrap-up disposition: e4faafbdbde434438d5c7d0d76f1fe9137dc00c5, Caught, no follow-up.
